named_duties: A FAILED AUDIT IS THE USEFUL RESULT. If the Minkowski-type bound forces exponent 1/3, L1 is CLOSED and the ceiling argument is a real contribution -- write it as one, with the argument in full, not as a disappointment. Section 8 exists because cheap pre-compute falsification is worth more than an expensive experiment on a dead lever.

STATE THE LATTICE PRECISELY BEFORE ARGUING ABOUT IT. Rank, determinant/discriminant, the quadratic form, and where each comes from. The paper's own Section 4.2 states that Hom(E, E^{(p)}) with the form deg is isometric to the two-sided ideal P of reduced norm p in the corresponding maximal order with the form Nrd/p -- start there, quote it, and do not substitute a remembered lattice for the stated one.

DISTINGUISH THE THREE QUANTITIES that are easy to conflate: (i) the PROVEN upper bound (p/2)^{1/3} for all E; (ii) the TYPICAL minimal degree for random E; (iii) any LOWER bound forcing a floor. A ceiling on L1 needs (iii), and (ii) is not (iii). If the literature gives only (i) and (ii), say exactly that and mark L1 UNRESOLVED rather than closed.

NEARBY-OBJECT CONTROL. If a bound closes E -> E^{(p)}, check whether the same argument closes the nearby targets a lever might substitute (other Galois conjugates, twists, small-degree-modified targets). A ceiling that applies to one object but not its neighbours is a redirection, not a closure -- record which.

L4: GET THE PUBLISHED PAPER OR RECORD THAT YOU COULD NOT. KN-TECH-058 records that two retrievals under KN-LIT-078's identifiers returned two different abstracts, one with no p^{1/4} figure at all, and that the descent structure was taken from ar5iv's rendering of arXiv:1310.7789 and is unverified for the published DCC version. Log every URL, timestamp, HTTP status and SHA-256 in source_access_log.yaml. If the paper cannot be obtained, that is a recorded outcome and NOT a mathematical finding.

DO NOT UPGRADE A CONFIDENCE LABEL WITHOUT THE PRIMARY TEXT. 'Two sources agree' is not the primary text. Absence of a stable source is not evidence the figure is wrong, either -- do not downgrade on absence.

Never fabricate a theorem, a bound, a constant, a citation or a retrieval. An unobtained source is recorded as unobtained.
